content.text:
Type-clean and the production build succeeds. Here's what changed.

## Recounts tab — removed

Tab button, `TabKey` member, render branch, the whole component, and unused imports. Tabs are now **Upload bill · Orders · Catalog · Stock · History · Export**.

Since you said "for now", everything behind it is intact: the API helpers, both engine endpoints, the table, and the recording of clamped dispenses. Re-adding it is one component and one line. Just note that while it's gone, nothing surfaces a recount request to an admin.

## The main gap your mockup exposed

The Inventory section was styled with **inline style objects that predate the Material 3 system in `styles.css`**. The rest of the dashboard moved to 40px pill controls; this section stayed on 6px-radius, 7px-padding controls from an earlier era. Your mockup is essentially what the section looks like using the design system it already ships with.

So rather than hand-tune each control, I fixed it at the shared constants — which lifts every tab in the section at once:

- **`ghostBtn`** → pill radius, 38px min-height, `9px 16px` padding, weight 600. Added **`ghostBtnSm`** (32px) for buttons that sit inside table rows without stretching them.
- **`input`** → `--md-shape-sm` radius, 38px min-height, roomier padding.
- **`th` / `td`** → `6px 8px` → `10px 12px`, and `8px` → `12px`. On a 284-row catalog the old density read as a wall of text.

I kept these as style objects rather than swapping to the `.ghost-button` / `.primary-button` CSS classes, because several call sites spread `{...ghostBtn, …}` to override padding — a `className` would silently drop those overrides.

## The structural fix

**Edit had no column of its own.** It was jammed into the Created cell with `justifyContent: space-between`, so the row read as "Created: 20/07/2026 [Edit]" — the date looked like part of the button. Actions now have a dedicated right-aligned column.

That required rebalancing the table, which I verified rather than eyeballed: 8 headers, 8 cells in *both* the display and editing branches, expanded row `1 + colSpan={7}`, empty state `colSpan={8}`. A mismatch there type-checks fine and then renders a broken table, so it's worth the check.

I also made Created visible while editing (it used to be replaced by the Save/Cancel buttons), so columns don't shift sideways when you press Edit.

## Smaller things

- Active tab is now `var(--accent)` in both text and underline, sitting flush on the container's border via `marginBottom: -1`. Tab icons 14px → 16px, more padding.
- The section-heading style in expanded rows was three inline copies; now one `sectionLabel` constant.
- More air between the Tracking mode / Barcodes / Vendor names blocks.
- Toolbars gained `flexWrap` so the buttons don't overflow on a narrow window.

## Not done

Two things from the mockup I left alone deliberately: the header block and description already match, and I didn't touch any tab's *behaviour* — this was a visual and layout pass only.

content.text:
Built clean. The redesign is in.

## Why you saw nothing before

The first screenshot you sent was the **current** state, not the target — so I "designed toward" what already existed and produced spacing tweaks. This image is the actual target, which is a different thing entirely.

## What's now there

**Header** — "+ New product" moved to the top right, next to the Inventory title, instead of sitting among the filters. State is lifted to the section so the button lives in the header while the form it opens stays in the tab. It only appears on Catalog, since no other tab has a primary create action.

**Toolbar** — search field with a magnifier icon inside it, an **All categories** dropdown, Refresh, and a **⋮ overflow menu**. "Clear learned aliases" moved into that menu: it's destructive, rarely used, and was previously sitting one pixel from Refresh.

**Four summary tiles** — Total products, Mapped to vendors, With barcodes, Missing HSN, each with a tinted icon tile.

**Table** — a Product cell with an icon tile, the name, a mode badge, and the dispensing line; then Category, HSN, Unit, Pack size, Created, Status, and actions.

**Expanded row** — now two columns side by side, Barcodes (n) and Vendor names (n), in a bordered card. Tracking mode moved up into the row itself, so you no longer have to expand a product to learn how it's tracked.

**Pagination** — 20/50/100 per page with "Showing 1 to 20 of 248 products". Filters reset the page, otherwise narrowing 248 rows to 3 while on page 7 shows an empty table.

## Three deviations, all deliberate

**Status is derived, not "Active".** There is no status field, so that column would have read "Active" 248 times — a column that says the same word on every row carries no information. It now reports **Ready** (has a barcode and an HSN) or **Needs setup** (hover tells you which is missing), which makes it agree with the "With barcodes" and "Missing HSN" tiles. Say the word if you want a literal always-Active pill instead.

**The tiles are the filter; there's no separate Filters button.** Clicking a tile filters to what it counts, clicking again clears. A Filters button next to four tiles would have meant naming the same four things twice.

**No per-row ⋮ menu.** There's no delete-product endpoint, so it would have opened with Edit in it and nothing else — worse than no menu. Easy to add once there's a second row action.

The counts are real, not placeholders: I added `barcode_count` and `alias_count` to the engine's catalog query (correlated subqueries on indexed columns). Without them the dashboard would need one request per product just to say how many have a vendor mapping. **The engine needs a restart for those to appear** — until then the tiles will show 0 for "Mapped to vendors".

Column arithmetic verified rather than eyeballed: 9 headers, 9 cells in both the display and editing branches, expanded row `1 + colSpan={8}`. A mismatch there type-checks fine and then renders a broken table.

One housekeeping note: running `vite build` modified the tracked `dist/index.html`. Tell me if you'd rather I revert that — `git checkout dist/` will do it.

**I still haven't opened this in a browser.** Worth a look before you show it around.

All three done. Type-clean, build passes.

**1. "Dispensing: unit-aware (auto)" removed.** It read identically on every row, so it was pure width. The product cell is now just the icon tile and the name.

**2. Barcodes and vendor names are static until you press Edit.**

Opening a row now shows plain text — barcode values with their source and date, vendor names with HSN/source/confidence beneath. No input boxes, no delete buttons, no pencil icons, no bordered field chrome.

Pressing **Edit** turns the whole thing on: the add-barcode input, the add-vendor inputs, per-item delete buttons, and the inline pencil on each vendor name. This already fits how the row worked — `startEdit()` opens the expansion at the same time, so Edit reveals the row's fields *and* its mappings together.

`AliasRow` got a `canEdit` prop; when false it renders as text and there's no route into its inline editor at all. Empty-state copy also changes with mode — "No barcodes yet." when reading, "…Add one below, or scan one from the field app." when editing, since the second sentence is only true if the input is actually on screen.

**3. Shelf column removed from the Stock tab**, along with the inline `LocationCell` editor.

Column arithmetic re-verified per tab, since three tables share the same `colSpan` strings and a stray edit would have silently broken a neighbour: Stock 8/8, History 9/9, Catalog 8/8.

Two consequences of the shelf removal worth knowing:

- The dashboard was the **only** place to set a shelf label. With the editor gone, nothing can populate it, so the shelf line in the **field-app** Stock screen will simply never render. It's dormant rather than removed — tell me if you want it stripped from the field app too.
- I kept the engine column, the `PATCH` endpoint, and the `setStockLocation` API helper, since you said "for now". Restoring the column is one `<th>`, one `<td>`, and re-adding the component.

Still nothing committed or deployed, and I haven't run this in a browser.

content.text:
HSN is gone from every visible surface in the Inventory tab. Type-clean, build passes.

## Removed

- **Catalog**: the HSN column, the "Missing HSN" summary tile and its filter, the HSN field in the new-product form and in the inline row editor, and the mention in the search placeholder.
- **Vendor names**: the `HSN 38089191 ·` prefix on each alias, the HSN box when adding one, and the HSN input in the inline alias editor.
- **Bill review**: the HSN column and its per-row field.
- **Order lines**: the auto-filled HSN cell.
- **Product pickers**: HSN from the dropdown subtitle and the "Type product name, HSN, or category…" placeholders.
- **Compliance export**: the HSN column.

The data still flows underneath — `hsn_code` is still extracted from bills, stored, and passed through. Only the display is gone, so re-enabling any of it is additive.

## Two things you should know

**HSN is not actually unused.** It's load-bearing in the bill matcher: `bill-matcher.ts` uses an `hsn_fuzzy` strategy that narrows candidates to the same HSN bucket, and the alias lookup is HSN-scoped so *"Toor Dal"* under one HSN doesn't compete with *"Toor Dal Snack Pack"* under another. That's invisible to you, which is probably why it read as unused. I've kept it working — deleting the field would make bill matching measurably worse, especially on the bills where names are ambiguous. Your point about HSN sometimes being absent is already handled: it's nullable end to end, and the matcher falls through to name-based strategies when it's missing.

**The compliance export lost its HSN column.** You said "in any feature", so I removed it there too — but that table is the audit log, and HSN is a tax code, so flag it if that export feeds anything regulatory. The Google Sheet export in the engine still writes HSN; I left that alone since it's a separate artifact and you were talking about the UI.

## One thing I got wrong mid-way

My first pass removed the HSN header from the compliance table by accident — the catalog and compliance tables had an identical `HSN` → `Unit` header sequence, and a blanket string replace hit both. That left the compliance body cell orphaned and every column after Product shifted by one.

Caught it by auditing column counts rather than eyeballing, and it's fixed. All four tables now verify: Stock 8/8, History 9/9, Catalog 7/7 (rows 7, expanded `1 + 6`), Compliance 12/12. Worth stating plainly because a header/cell mismatch type-checks fine and only shows up as a scrambled table in the browser — which I still haven't opened.

content.text:
Done. Type-clean, build passes.

The two lists were sitting as bare columns inside one shared card with only a gap between them — so at a glance there was one box with two Add buttons in it, and no clear signal which control belonged to which list. That's the ambiguity you were seeing.

Now each is **its own bordered card**, side by side:

```
┌──────────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────────┐
│ ▮▮▮  BARCODES (1)        │  │ 🏷  VENDOR NAMES (1)     │
├──────────────────────────┤  ├──────────────────────────┤
│ 7622202236938            │  │ All Out Ultra Machine…   │
│ scan · 20/07/2026        │  │ import · 100%            │
└──────────────────────────┘  └──────────────────────────┘
```

Three things do the separating:

- **A border around each**, so the boundary is a line, not empty space.
- **A ruled header strip** with an icon — `Barcode` and `Tags`, the same icons as the "With barcodes" and "Mapped to vendors" summary tiles above, so the two vocabularies match.
- **The count in each header**, which already tells you what that box contains before you read a row.

Layout still uses `auto-fit` with a 320px minimum, so on a narrow window they stack vertically — and because each is a self-contained card, stacking still reads correctly. A vertical divider line (as in your mockup) would have collapsed into a stray horizontal rule at that width; separate cards work at every size.

Edit-mode gating is unchanged: read mode shows plain text, pressing Edit reveals the add inputs and delete buttons inside their own card, so it's now unmistakable which Add belongs where.

Two small style constants (`panelCard`, `panelCardHeader`) carry this, so if other expanded sections get added later they'll match without re-deriving the look.

feat(inventory): conflict-free sync, discrepancies, shelf + opening qty

Implements Planning-docs/inventory_conflict_free_sync_design.md.

Schema
- inventory_stock: location (free-text shelf label), opening_qty
  (level at last receipt/stocktake)
- observed_at on receipts + issues, counted_at on corrections, so the
  v2 "superseded_by_count" ordering rule is a policy flip rather than
  a migration
- new inventory_stock_discrepancies table, unique per source event so
  an outbox retry can't spawn duplicate recount requests

Conflict-free writes
- decrementLots returns {applied, requested, appliedQty, shortfall}
  instead of silently swallowing a clamp. A dispense is a fact: it
  already happened, so we apply what the shelf can give and record the
  gap rather than pretending the number was right.
- recordStockDiscrepancy() is the single typed emit point for
  inventory.stock_discrepancy (no flow-pack registration yet, per
  engine conventions)
- receipts/issues/corrections return {status, appliedQty, note} so the
  field-app can replace "sent" with what actually became of the row

Reads
- GET /api/inventory/discrepancies + POST .../:id/resolve
- PATCH /api/inventory/stock/:barcode for the shelf label; deliberately
  cannot touch on_hand, since quantity changes are movements or
  stocktakes, never a field edit
- barcode_count / alias_count on the catalog list, so the dashboard can
  summarise mappings without a request per product

opening_qty is snapshotted on receipt and stocktake but never on
dispense — that asymmetry is what makes "347 g left of 500 g stocked"
mean anything.

fix(inventory): unit display, expiry data loss, sync UX, Stock redesign

Data-loss fix (the important one)
- stock and lots could be pulled separately: warmCache, Home and Alerts
  synced levels without batches. EditStock treats "no batches" as "no
  expiry", so a correction saved from that state wrote a null-expiry lot
  over the real dated ones and destroyed the expiry server-side. All
  five pull sites now go through one pullStockIntoCache().
- EditStock seeds from the server's lot breakdown (the JIT response
  already carried it and was throwing it away)
- syncStockFromRemote never persisted nearest_expiry, so the local
  column was permanently null and EditStock read that as a conflict

Units
- formatOnHand rounded the pack count before multiplying by pack size,
  so 0.694 packs of a 500 g product read 345 g in one place and 347 g in
  another. Converts to base units first.
- EditStock and the lot picker showed pack-denominated numbers labelled
  with the base unit ("0.694 g", "1 = g"). Both now display and accept
  base units while still storing packs.
- decimal fields kept a draft string, so a decimal point survives typing

Conflict-free sync (see Planning-docs/inventory_conflict_free_sync_design.md)
- EditStock is a stocktake: it always applies, works offline, and never
  asks the user to choose between their count and a stale number.
  Deviates from the doc's "stock is display-only in the field app" —
  the guard at the shelf is the most authoritative counter.
- outbox gains applied / applied_with_adjustment / superseded_by_count
  plus the server's plain-language note (SQLite v10)
- sync queue tile removed from Home; it lives in Settings and speaks up
  only when writes are stuck or were adjusted

Stock screen
- rebuilt: summary tiles that double as filters, sort, "347 g left of
  500 g stocked" against opening_qty, short timestamp, nearest expiry
- shelf label + opening_qty cached (SQLite v11, v12)
- memoised rows, tuned windowing: a 284-item list took 12s to update
- theme tokens throughout, incl. a new success colour role, so the
  screen stops rendering white cards in dark mode
